looks like there was more than just KEY's done

The original intention with using these enum types everywhere was to improve the typing when using languages such as C#. I'm not an expert on C++ enums so I don't know what's the best approach here (though I know that just using `int` everywhere is sub-optimal, and now I see that using the enum everywhere is also bad due to UB).

Are there disadvantages to `enum class`? It seems like it's an overall nicer option, so maybe we should use it in more places. From what I can see, members are scoped to the enum instead of having the same scope as the enum (so we wouldn't need WHATEVER_ prefixes on all members), and it seems less prone to undefined behavior.
See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2854. Enum classes are generally considered good practice by modern C++ standards, so I would vouch for using them in 4.0 too.

Ok, I've started working on this for the past hour. Good news: These enum classes are indeed a lot nicer, the code that works so far is looking nice, and another piece of good news is that this is a really good way to catch places that aren't using the enum but should. Bad news: This is going to take *forever*, hopefully not more than the weekend, but I need to fix >100 files.

review_comments: In order to make `enum class` work with the current binding system, Variant has to know about the enum classes. With the input enums it's simple to just include the files inside of Variant. If we want to do this with other enums, we may need to move them to minimal files that we can include in Variant.
What are these constructors needed for?
Can you link me the location in code? I want to see if this can be done differently.
Ah, I understand now. `VariantCaster` is only one way, unlike `PtrToArg`. To convert back to Variant, we rely on those constructors. This looks fine then.
This may change behavior, but I think that the old code may have been a mistake. -1 is not part of the enum. ` MouseButton::NONE` is 0.
I added this helper inline function, `mouse_button_to_mask`. This should improve readability.
